title: Perf regression canary (prod) — project notes / running log
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-2841 (Perf regression canary in prod)
Confluence (ADR draft): baseline strategy (rolling vs pinned known-good)
content:
Last updated: 2026-02-12 (Marcus)

Purpose of this doc
- Working area for running notes + early decisions + open questions.
- Not the “final” design doc; Confluence will hold the canonical spec once we’re done iterating.
- If you’re looking for the work plan / owners: see Linear ENG-2841.

Quick links
- Linear epic: ENG-2841
- Draft metric spec: (Confluence draft; Nadia/Logan)
- Workload matrix sheet: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/perf-canary-workload-matrix-sheet.json
- Canary repo: github.com/redwood/perf-canary (PR #102 / #109 etc.)
- Runtime tags PR: redwood PR #39122

TL;DR (current direction)
- We will run a low-QPS “perf-canary” workload per region, per model, with a fixed workload matrix (prompt shapes + token budgets) that is stable enough to trend.
- Primary signals in v1:
  1) p95 end-to-end latency (separate for streaming vs non-streaming)
  2) tokens/sec (decode throughput) (streaming fix required)
- Regression detector compares to rolling baseline (7d median) with deploy-window suppression + minimum sample size guardrails.
- Canary traffic is tagged end-to-end (source=perf-canary) and uses “canary-safe” request class so we don’t fight customer queues.

What success looks like (first cut)
- Detect p95 latency regressions of ~8–12% and tokens/sec regressions of ~8–12% for covered slices within <= 30–60 minutes, with < 1 page/week false-positive rate during steady state.
- When an alert fires, payload must answer:
  - which model/region/gpu_sku/runtime_build/scheduler_mode
  - how large is regression (value + %)
  - baseline reference (rolling 7d vs pinned)
  - recent deploy annotations / runtime SHA
  - links: dashboard + runbook + “what changed” diff pointer

Non-goals (reminder)
- Not a customer-facing perf SLA product (v1 is internal).
- Not a replacement for benchmark lab.
- Not covering every possible model parameter / prompt distribution.


Decisions log (rough)

2025-12-19 — Canary traffic isolation
- Decision (tentative): Use a distinct request class (“canary-safe”) with strict rate limit + low priority + concurrency cap.
- Rationale: dedicated queue is cleaner but adds operational surface area; request class gives us most of the isolation benefits quickly.
- Owners: Sofia (scheduler), Omar (instrumentation).
- Follow-up: confirm we can pin scheduler mode (see notes below) so variance doesn’t eat us.

2026-01-06 — Allowed label schema (cardinality)
- Decision: metrics labels limited to:
  - model
  - region
  - gpu_sku (coarse buckets only; no host ids)
  - runtime_build (short build id / release train id)
  - scheduler_mode (enum; no arbitrary strings)
  - canary_variant (small enum: e.g., “streaming”, “nonstreaming”, “longprefill”, “shortprefill”)
- Not allowed:
  - kernel_id as a label (too high cardinality)
  - request_id / host_id labels
- Kernel selection info must be attached as:
  - debug logs sampled or emitted only in alert payload / trace
  - or as a low-cardinality “kernel_family” enum (TBD) if we can justify.
- Reference: discussion with Logan/Nadia + Thomas Baird (cardinality controls).

2026-01-09 — Baseline strategy (still not 100% final)
- Direction: rolling 7d median baseline, plus option to pin to known-good runtime_build for investigations.
- Deploy/maintenance suppression required; otherwise we’ll page ourselves during rollouts.
- Pending: ADR writeup in Confluence (Allison + Sean reviewing).

2026-01-15 — Streaming tokens/sec definition
- Found mismatch between “first token timestamp” definitions (runtime vs telemetry). Fix in progress.
- Action: align on: tokens/sec = total_generated_tokens / (t_last_token - t_first_token) for streaming, with guardrails if only 1 token.
- Related PRs: redwood PR #39157 (fix) + telemetry pipeline check.

2026-01-28 — Warmup/cache priming
- Decision: include a small warmup phase per model per region after deploy annotation changes (or runtime restart).
- We will NOT include warmup requests in baseline/regression windows.
- TBD: whether to prime KV/prefix cache intentionally (pros: stability; cons: hides cache-related regressions).


Open questions (keep updated; please add your name if you own one)

Q1) Workload representativeness vs stability
- We need stable slices for detection, but don’t want to overfit to synthetic prompts.
- Proposed compromise:
  - v1 matrix uses canonical prompt shapes per model family (short/long prefill; short/long decode) + fixed max_new_tokens.
  - v2 adds a “realistic distribution” lane from anonymized synthetic prompts that mimic production histograms.
- Owner: Noah + Marcus.

Q2) GPU heterogeneity handling
- Do we always split by gpu_sku? Concern: if we don’t, regressions get averaged away; if we do, we multiply time series.
- Current: split by gpu_sku for top SKUs only (A100-80G, H100-80G, L40S) and “other”.
- Need: exact mapping + where it lives (runtime label vs telemetry enrichment).
- Owner: Logan + Caleb.

Q3) Kernel selection attribution
- We want “kernel id + fallback reason” when the alert fires, but not as a metric label.
- Options:
  (a) write a small “kernel selection snapshot” event to tracing span for canary requests
  (b) emit to logs only when a regression is suspected (hard)
  (c) always log for canary, but sampling
- Owner: Hiro + Omar.

Q4) Batching / scheduler variance bias
- Canary traffic can be affected by mixing with other traffic (even with low priority) and by dynamic batching heuristics.
- Sofia suggested pinning scheduler config for canary requests (disable experimental heuristic X) to reduce variance.
- Need to confirm if pinning reduces variance without masking real regressions.
- Owner: Sofia.

Q5) Noise handling without hiding real incidents
- Outlier filtering: remove node-level contention spikes? If we filter too hard, we could miss “real” regressions caused by contention.
- Proposed: keep raw series visible; for alerting use a robust estimator + minimum sample size; annotate with “contention suspected” if queue time spikes.
- Owner: Sean + Nadia.


Workstreams / current status (informal)

A) Runner service (perf-canary)
- Status: implemented skeleton (config + model list loader + modes). PR #102 up.
- Next:
  - add region routing config
  - implement warmup steps
  - add rate limiting / canary-safe auth
  - ensure request tagging is consistent with runtime (source=perf-canary)
- Owner: Marcus.

B) Runtime instrumentation hooks
- Status:
  - runtime_build + scheduler_mode propagation in PR #39122
  - batch composition stats proposal in review
- Needed in v1 payload/context:
  - runtime_build (release train id) + git sha
  - scheduler_mode (enum)
  - batch stats (prefill/decode counts, max seq len, maybe effective batch size)
  - kv cache metrics (hit rate? cautious on cardinality)
- Owner: Omar + Julian.

C) Metrics spec + pipeline
- Status: draft spec in progress; label schema mostly agreed.
- Metrics to lock down:
  - latency_p95_ms (for streaming: “time to last token” AND “time to first token” are separate signals; confirm which we alert on)
  - tokens_per_sec_p50 (or p95?) — if we use p95 for throughput it can be weird; might use median to avoid tail noise
  - sample_count
  - error_rate (so we don’t misread failures as perf improvements)
- Owner: Nadia + Logan.

D) Regression detection + suppression
- Status: initial approach drafted.
- Guardrails we keep repeating because we’ll forget:
  - minimum N requests per window (per slice)
  - ignore first X minutes after deploy annotation change
  - suppression during maintenance windows + active rollouts (regional)
  - require regression to persist for >= 2 windows (or 2/3 rule) before paging
- Owner: Sean + Rafael (integration) + Nadia (math).

E) Dashboards
- Status: Felix started mockups; needs consistent annotation events.
- Must-have panels:
  - per model: p95 latency + tokens/sec (stream vs non-stream)
  - heatmap across regions/gpu
  - table of “top regressions in last 24h” with links
  - deploy annotations: runtime_build + git sha
- Owner: Felix.


Draft metrics notes (very rough; not canonical)

Latency
- We need to disambiguate:
  - non-streaming: end-to-end latency = t_response_end - t_request_start
  - streaming:
    - TTFT (time to first token): t_first_token - t_request_start (often correlates with prefill)
    - TTLC (time to last chunk / completion): t_last_token - t_request_start
- For v1 paging: probably TTFT p95 + tokens/sec regression (decode) are the two most actionable.
- But customers complain in “total time” too; keep TTLC visible on dashboards.

Tokens/sec
- Must use consistent tokenization + definition of start/end timestamps.
- Streaming gotcha: if the first chunk includes metadata / tool call, timestamp alignment can be off.
- Action item: standardize how we mark “first token” in runtime span.

Batching bias
- Tokens/sec can improve if batch size increases (or if requests coalesce). Canary is low volume so this can swing.
- We might need a “target concurrency” per slice to stabilize batching behavior.
- Alternative: do not depend on batching, run canary in isolation queue (later).


Meeting notes / snippets

2026-01-15 Internal sync (Runtime + SRE + Telemetry)
- Sean: please don’t page on the first week; start in ticket-first mode and backtest.
- Logan: label schema must be locked before we ship; retrofitting is painful.
- Noah: baseline should be rolling; pinned known-good is for debugging, not the default.
- Sofia: scheduler pinning for canary requests is acceptable if it’s clearly tagged.
- Action items:
  - Marcus: add “canary_variant” enum to config so we can group windows cleanly.
  - Nadia: propose thresholds for phase 1 (us-east, 2–3 models).
  - Omar: confirm runtime_build tag is present at the metric emission site (not lost in aggregation).

2026-01-27 Notes to self (Marcus)
- The hardest part is not generating load; it’s making the time series trustworthy.
- If we can’t make noise manageable, we should reduce coverage instead of loosening thresholds.
- Need to keep “signal quality” checks front and center: sample size, error rate, queue time.


Near-term TODOs (next 1–2 weeks)
- [ ] Finalize initial model list for phase 1 (2–3 models) + regions (us-east only) — align with Noah/Sofia
- [ ] Lock metric names + definitions (Nadia/Logan) and document in Confluence spec
- [ ] Confirm runtime emits: runtime_build, scheduler_mode, gpu_sku (or equivalent) for canary traffic
- [ ] Implement warmup handling + exclude warmup from alert windows
- [ ] Backtest detector on historical windows (Nadia + Sean)
- [ ] Draft runbook “what to do first” checklist (Tomáš + Sean) and link from dashboard + incident-bot

Appendix: proposed initial coverage (not final)
- Region: us-east
- Models: (placeholder; confirm with Noah)
  - llama-3.1-70b-instruct (popular, sensitive)
  - qwen2.5-72b-instruct (different kernel path)
  - small model lane (e.g., llama-3.1-8b) for high-frequency sampling
- Canary variants (enum)
  - v_short: prefill 128, decode 64
  - v_longprefill: prefill 2048, decode 64
  - v_longdecode: prefill 256, decode 512
  - streaming/non-streaming for each

Appendix: questions for Confluence design doc
- Where exactly do we compute p95: telemetry pipeline vs runtime? (prefer pipeline; runtime only emits histograms)
- What do we consider “baseline”: 7d median at same time-of-day? (maybe later)
- How do we annotate deploy windows reliably across regions? (Connor coordinating release annotations)
